=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: around line 5690 in the new `security_pass_file_deferred_advisory_followups` function (the `jq … > "${STATE_FILE}.tmp" || ! mv "${STATE_FILE}.tmp" "${STATE_FILE}"` block that settles the waiver row after a successful create)
  Problem: The `if ! jq … || ! mv …; then … fi` pattern has inverted truth-table semantics. The intent is "if jq fails, try to roll back the rename; if either step fails, enter the warning branch". With `||` and `!`, the expression evaluates to false (skips the branch) precisely when jq fails AND mv succeeds — which is the case that silently leaves a corrupt STATE_FILE on disk. Specifically: when jq exits non-zero, jq's stdout to `${STATE_FILE}.tmp` is empty/garbled; mv then overwrites the real state file with that empty/garbled content; `! mv` is then 1; the `||` produces 1; `if ! 1` is false; the warning branch is skipped, no `rm -f tmp`, no warning, and the next poll reads a corrupt state.
  Why it fails at runtime: The poller is the only writer of `${STATE_FILE}`. A transient jq failure on the merged-state tick — malformed state JSON, a syntax-level jq regression, or a resource hiccup — corrupts the project's `security_pass_waived_findings` (the very ledger this PR's deferral machinery relies on). The very rows the new function was written to settle (`followup_pending: true`, `audited_head_sha`, `finding`) are lost, and the next run's `pending_json` selection returns an empty list, so the deferred advisory is never filed even though `create_security_pass_advisory_followup` returned a real issue number on the line above. The same `jq || ! mv` shape is also present in `create_security_pass_advisory_followup` at the `existing_issue` reconciliation (around line 5521) and the post-create state write (around line 5623); both pre-existing instances will exhibit the same silent corruption. Fix: split the write and the rename into two explicit checks (e.g. `if ! jq … > tmp; then rm -f tmp; echo ::warning::; continue; fi; mv tmp state`) so a failed jq never silently overwrites the state file. Apply consistently at all three call sites.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

- File: scripts/implement_staged_support_workspace.sh
  Location: `_unsafe_path()` (lines 78-83)
  Issue: the case pattern rejects `/*`, `../*`, `*/../*`, `..`, `*/..` but not the bare `.` (or `./`). If such an entry ever reached the ledger, `git restore --source=HEAD --worktree -- .` would restore the entire worktree to HEAD, silently discarding all uncommitted editor edits and turning the run into a no-op. The ledger is machine-generated by the staging step so this cannot occur in practice, but the guard's stated contract is fail-closed on unsafe ledger paths and this is the one destructive relative path it misses.
  Suggested minimal fix: extend the pattern in `_unsafe_path()` to `/*|../*|*/../*|..|*/..|.|./)` (same change mirrored in the identical case in scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:165-166 if consistency is desired).
